nodes.name: Execute Workflow Trigger
nodes.notes: Lets Agent 6 (or any caller) invoke this workflow directly via Execute Workflow, bypassing HMAC verification since it's an internal n8n-to-n8n call. Feeds the same {leadId, orgId, templateId, enrollmentId} shape into IF: Sending Enabled that Verify Signature produces for the webhook path.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify((() => { const m = $('GET Agent Prompt (writer)').first().json.agent.model; const model = (!m || /nemotron|openrouter/i.test(m)) ? 'gemini-3.5-flash-lite' : m; const isGemma = /^gemma/i.test(model); const body = { model, max_tokens: isGemma ? Math.max(512, 4096) : 512, messages: [{role:'system', content: $('GET Agent Prompt (writer)').first().json.agent.systemPrompt}, {role:'user', content: JSON.stringify({ lead: $('GET Lead').first().json.lead, template: $('GET Template').first().json.template })}] }; return body; })()) }}

nodes.name: Postmark: Send Email
nodes.notes: IMPORTANT: was completely unauthenticated (no credential, no token header) despite the old 'predefinedCredentialType'/'postmarkApi' config below implying otherwise -- that credential type was never actually backed by a real credential in this n8n instance (confirmed via list_credentials: zero Postmark credentials ever existed), so it silently had no effect. Also built its body via bodyParameters (n8n's form-encoded/keypair path) while declaring a content-type: application/json header -- the two contradicted each other and Postmark's API would reject the mismatched body regardless of auth. And it never included a From address at all, which Postmark requires (a verified Sender Signature on the account). Fixed all three: a real X-Postmark-Server-Token header sourced from $vars.POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN (matching this project's convention for every other third-party API key -- TAVILY_API_KEY, HUNTER_API_KEY, APOLLO_API_KEY, GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY -- rather than n8n's credential store), a real specifyBody:"json" body, and From sourced from $vars.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL. Both variables must be set by a human in n8n's Variables settings with real values from a verified Postmark account before this can actually send -- see README.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ From: $vars.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL, To: $('GET Lead').first().json.lead.email, Subject: $json.subject, TextBody: $json.body, MessageStream: 'outbound' }) }}

nodes.name: Check Postmark Result
nodes.notes: Postmark can return HTTP 200 with a non-zero ErrorCode in its response body (e.g. an inactive recipient) -- checking HTTP status alone isn't enough to know the send actually succeeded.
